question.leadin: This group mocked the US, France, and UK forces during a mock funeral in Khost.
question.text: Name this group that took over a certain country after defeating a resistance movement in Panjshir Province. This group, which takes its name from the word "students," is largely led by Pashtun militants.
question.clue: This group, the main opponent of the Northern Alliance, carried out the "green on blue" attacks.

swap.text: This man was the greatest expander of the Mongol Empire, conquering territory across China and Central Asia.
swap.clue: He also defeated both the Xi Xia and Jin Dynasties, and after his death, he was succeeded not by Jochi or Chatagai, but by his third son, Ogodai.

question.leadin: Give the following about the 1449 Tumu [tuh-MU] Crisis.
question.text: The crisis involved a raid of 20,000 of these people, led by Esen Taishi, into Ming territory where they destroyed an unprepared army of half a million Ming soldiers. These people ruled the Yuan Dynasty, which was defeated by the Ming.
question.clue: A non-Byzantine Secret History chronicles the rise of these people's first leader, who was born with the name Temujin.

swap.leadin: The southern branch of this route went through the Karakoram (KEH-ruh-koh-rum) mountains.
swap.text: Name this trade route that connected China with several Eurasian empires, named for a coveted textile.
swap.clue: In the plural, this term was subtitled A New History of the World in a work by Peter Frankopan, and it names Yo-Yo Ma's ensemble to promote cross-cultural artistic collaboration.

question.leadin: Items such as an entire Quran inscribed within a ring were produced during this conqueror's namesake "Renaissance."
question.text: Name this Uzbek (OOZ-bek) warlord who, from his capital of Samarkand (SAA-mark-and), assembled an empire stretching from Delhi to Damascus in the late 14th century.
question.answerHtml: Tamerlane (TAM-er-lain) [or Tamerlame; or Timur the Lame; or Timūr Gurkānī; or Temür Küregen]
question.clue: After detaining an envoy sent by the Emperor Hongwu, he led a short lived expedition against the Ming Dynasty.

swap.text: This narrow mountain pass through the Durand Line is the main route between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Babur attacked India through this pass to start the Mughal dynasty.
swap.clue: Famously crossed by Alexander the Great, Darius I, and Genghis Khan, this pass links Pakistan and Afghanistan and was an integral part of the Silk Road.

question.leadin: Mullah Fazlullah became the leader of this group in 2013, which has claimed responsibility for attacks like the 2016 Bacha Khan University attack and 2014 Peshawar school attack.
question.text: Name this terrorist group which has broken up into the Ahrar-ul-Hind, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, and South Waziristan factions. A similarly named group in a neighboring country was once led by Mohammed Omar.
question.answerHtml: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan [Accept TTP or Pakistani Taliban, prompt on Taliban by asking “in which country”]

swap.leadin: This empire was formed in the 7th century AD following the end of the Zhangzhung kingdom.
swap.text: Name this ancient Himalayan empire which flourished until the 9th century and had a capital at Lhasa.
swap.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.

question.leadin: Qazi ("kah-zi") Mullah led a state in this mountain range that was invaded during the Murid War.
question.text: Name this mountain range, where the Naqshbandi Sufi leader Imam Shamil led resistance to foreign occupation. The Circassian ethnic group is from this mountain range.
question.clue: Bagrationi Dynasty rulers such as Tamar the Great led a kingdom based in this range.The Circassians were based in this range, near the site of a genocide that remains ignored underArticle 301 today.

swap.leadin: Name these areas that were once independent from China.
swap.text: Called Bodyul in the native language and Xizang in Chinese, this area was taken from the Mongols in 1720 and has been under continuous Chinese control since a 1950 invasion.
swap.clue: This region's future was settled by a Seventeen Point Plan agreed to by representatives of a man who had been tutored by Heinrich Harrer.

question.text: The European Union suspended most diplomatic relations with Uzbekistan following the May 2005 incident in this city, where demonstrators were massacred by the army in Bobur Square after twenty-three accused terrorists broke out of prison.

swap.leadin: Joseph Wolff was spared from execution after a ruler of this city laughed at his missionary attire.
swap.text: Name this city where Nasrullah Khan had Arthur Conolly, the coiner of the phrase "Great Game," executed. A Central Asian Jewish diaspora named for this city became Russian subjects in 1865.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.leadin: A king from this city named Fromo Kesaro, or "Rome Caesar," commemorated his defeat of Yazid ibn Ziyad in his coinage.
question.text: Name this westernmost capital city home to a Turkic "Shahi" dynasty that expanded to Gandhara. The Turk Shahis likely used the "Bala Hissar" fort in this city, as did the later Hindu Shahis who lost to Mahmud of Ghazni.
question.clue: A government in this city was established through the Peshawar Accord after the fall of Mohammad Najibullah.

swap.text: One of the dynasties that sprung up in Transoxiana after the demise of the Abbasids was this one, whose founder Sabuktigin founded it by seizing Samanid territory. Its sultan Mahmud patronized the poet Ferdowsi.
swap.clue: This Islamic dynasty based out of Afghanistan that brought Islam to the heart of India under their greatest ruler Mahmud.

question.text: Paizas were often carried by messengers traveling along this Mongolian postal system, which contained relay stations with supplies, shelter, and spare horses.

swap.text: The leader of the Mongol forces, Hulagu Khan, was not with his army during the battle, as he was involved in a succession struggle following the death of this Khagan, or head khan, in 1259, while on campaign in China. He was the last person to have effective rule over all the Mongol hordes.
swap.clue: This ruler from the Toluid line subjected merchants to taxation and paid nobles in salaries as part of his administrative reform efforts.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.text: The Orkhon Valley is also home to the Erdene Zuu monastery, which was unfortunately smashed up in 1939 by this Communist leader called the "Stalin of Mongolia," as part of his program of destroying Buddhist sites.
swap.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

question.leadin: A member of this family abolished the longstanding beylik system in a series of westernizing reforms encouraged by his backer Catherine the Great.
question.text: Name this family whose founder supposedly devised a three-pronged symbol known as the Tarak Tamga. That man's son defeated the last Khan of the Golden Horde and occupied Sarai.
question.answerHtml: Giray [accept Hacı I Giray or Melek Haji Giray or Şahin Giray]

swap.leadin: The Rajputs defeated a ruler of this dynasty at the First Battle of Taraori, so he raised a bigger army, revised his tactics, went back the next year, and crushed them on the same battlefield.
swap.text: Identify this Persianate dynasty, originally from a namesake region in present-day Afghanistan, whose ruler Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad conquered the Ghaznavids by capturing Lahore in 1186 CE.
